- v3.0.0 (14 April 2026) added rotating webhook signing secrets without downtime.

detail.final_text:
On the Starter plan, your API rate limit is **120 requests per minute**.

This comes from Fernbird's "Rate limits and quotas" page (`/docs/rate-limits.html`). The docs index doesn't link to that page, so I found it with the docs search. It also says:

- **Per workspace:** the limit covers your whole workspace, not each key or user, and is counted over a sliding one-minute window.
- **Bursts:** you can go up to twice the limit (240 per minute) for 10 seconds.
- **Batch endpoints:** these count as one request for every 100 objects.
- **Going over:** you get a `429` error with a `Retry-After` header telling you how many seconds to wait.

The four newest changelog entries (back to 9 July 2026) don't mention any rate-limit changes. I didn't check the older pages.

For comparison, Team is 600 per minute and Team Plus is 1,200. Starter also allows only 2 webhook endpoints.

On the Starter plan, your API rate limit is **120 requests per minute**.

That figure comes from Fernbird's "Rate limits and quotas" page at `/docs/rate-limits.html`. The docs menu doesn't link to that page; I found it by trying likely URLs. Its plan table:

|---|---|---|
| **Starter** | **120** | 2 |
| Team | 600 | 10 |
| Team Plus | 1,200 | 25 |

- **Short bursts are allowed:** you can go up to twice the limit (240 requests per minute) for 10 seconds.
- **Batch endpoints count as one request per 100 objects.**
- **Going over the limit returns a `429` error with a `Retry-After` header.** The official SDKs retry 429 errors automatically.

The pricing page doesn't list rate limits. The changelog pages I checked (back to March 2026) don't mention any change to them, so this table looks current.

- You can burst up to twice the limit (240 requests per minute) for up to 10 seconds.
- Batch endpoints count as one request per 100 objects.
- Going over the limit returns a 429 error.

One batch request to the events endpoint can carry **at most 500 events**. A bigger batch gets **HTTP 413** with the error code `batch_too_large`.

This is from the Events section of the API reference, under `POST /events/batch`:

> "Record up to 500 events in one request. A larger batch is refused whole with 413 batch_too_large; split it and send the parts in order. For rate limits a batch counts as one request per 100 events."

A few things to watch for:
- **The whole batch is refused.** None of its events are recorded, so you have to split it and send the parts in order.
- **Messages have a lower limit.** `POST /messages/batch` takes at most 100, not 500.
- **A different 413 also exists.** The Errors section lists `413 payload_too_large` for any request body over 5 MB. So a batch of 500 events or fewer can still get a 413 if its body is too large (each event's `properties` can be up to 16 KB).

detail.final_text:
The current limit is **25 MB of attachments per message**, on every plan.

- **Source:** Fernbird's blog post ["Bigger attachments on every plan"](http://127.0.0.1:46621/blog/bigger-attachments.html), dated 2 June 2026. It raised the limit from 10 MB.
- **How it's counted:** The limit applies to the files as you send them, before encoding. So a 24 MB PDF fits, even though encoding makes it bigger in transit.
- **Inbound limits:** These didn't change.

The blog's "Most read" section still shows the older post, "Attachments are here" (May 2024), which says 10 MB. That figure is out of date. I also checked the changelog entries since June (July to September 2026) and none of them change the attachment limit again.

detail.final_text:
The current limit is **25 MB per message**, and it applies to every plan.

This comes from Fernbird's blog post "Bigger attachments on every plan" (2 June 2026, http://127.0.0.1:40019/blog/bigger-attachments.html). It raised the limit from the 10 MB announced in their May 2024 post "Attachments are here."

- **What counts toward the limit:** the files as you send them, before encoding. The post's example is that a 24 MB PDF now fits.
- **Received email:** the limits for incoming mail didn't change. The post doesn't say what they are.

The post was the latest one about attachments when I checked. The only newer post is "A home in the EU" (18 August 2026), which is about storing data in Frankfurt. The browser opened it and found nothing about attachment size, but I didn't read its full text myself.
